from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game"
        lines = [
            "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks.",
            "Rule one: move only one disk at a time.",
            "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one.",
            "Goal: move the stack to a different peg.",
            "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors
        COLOR_DISK1 = BLUE_B
        COLOR_DISK2 = GREEN_B
        COLOR_DISK3 = ORANGE
        COLOR_PEG = GRAY_B
        COLOR_HIGHLIGHT = YELLOW
        COLOR_INVALID = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "The Tower of Hanoi has three pegs and disks."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Pegs - using grid points for alignment
        peg_h = 3.2
        peg_a = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_b = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        peg_c = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=peg_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_PEG, stroke_width=0)
        
        self.place_at_grid(peg_a, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_b, "D3")
        self.place_at_grid(peg_c, "D5")
        
        labels = VGroup(
            Text("A", font_size=24),
            Text("B", font_size=24),
            Text("C", font_size=24)
        )
        labels[0].next_to(self.grid["F1"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[1].next_to(self.grid["F3"], DOWN, buff=0.1)
        labels[2].next_to(self.grid["F5"], DOWN, buff=0.1)

        # Disks
        disk_h = 0.5
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK3)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=1.3, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK2)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, width=0.8, height=disk_h, fill_opacity=1, color=COLOR_DISK1)
        
        # Stack disks on Peg A using grid slots
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "E1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "D1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C1")

        self.play(FadeIn(VGroup(peg_a, peg_b, peg_c)), Write(labels), FadeIn(VGroup(disk1, disk2, disk3)))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "Rule one: move only one disk at a time."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Animate top disk (Disk 1) moving from Peg A (C1) to Peg B (E3)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["E3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Rule two: no larger disk atop a smaller one."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Try to move Disk 2 on top of Disk 1 at Peg B
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D3"]), run_time=0.4)
        
        # Flash Red indicating invalid move
        flash_rect = SurroundingRectangle(disk2, color=COLOR_INVALID, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(flash_rect))
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_INVALID), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(disk2.animate.set_fill(COLOR_DISK2), run_time=0.2)
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_rect))
        
        # Return Disk 2 to Peg A
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B3"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.3)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["D1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "Goal: move the stack to a different peg."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Move Disk 2 to Peg C
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B1"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["B5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.play(disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["E5"]), run_time=0.4)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "Binary counting reveals the most efficient solution."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Highlight entire stack on A (Disk 3) and target Peg C
        highlight_a = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_a, disk3), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        highlight_c = SurroundingRectangle(VGroup(peg_c, disk2), color=COLOR_HIGHLIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(highlight_a), Create(highlight_c))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_a), FadeOut(highlight_c))
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard
        title = "Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse"
        lines = [
            "Binary counting uses a sequence of flipping bits.",
            "Each bit position represents a power of two.",
            "Observe which bit flips during each increment."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors for alignment
        COLOR_LINE1 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_LINE2 = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_LINE3 = "#00FFFF" # Cyan/Blue
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight Line 1
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE1))
        
        # Initial bits "000" in White
        bit3 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        bit2 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        bit1 = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        
        bits_group = VGroup(bit3, bit2, bit1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(bits_group, "B2", "C5")
        
        self.play(Write(bits_group))
        self.wait(0.5)
        
        # Transition 000 -> 001, rightmost bit yellow
        new_bit1_y = Text("1", font_size=60, color=COLOR_LINE1)
        new_bit1_y.move_to(bit1)
        
        self.play(Transform(bit1, new_bit1_y))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight Line 2
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE2)
        )
        
        # Labels for powers of 2 (4, 2, 1) in Green
        p3 = Text("2^2", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        p2 = Text("2^1", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        p1 = Text("2^0", font_size=24, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        
        # Position labels above bits
        p3.move_to(bit3.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        p2.move_to(bit2.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        p1.move_to(bit1.get_top() + UP * 0.6)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(p3), FadeIn(p2), FadeIn(p1))
        
        # Transition 001 -> 010, middle bit green
        new_bit2_g = Text("1", font_size=60, color=COLOR_LINE2)
        new_bit2_g.move_to(bit2)
        zero_bit1_w = Text("0", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        zero_bit1_w.move_to(bit1)
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit2, new_bit2_g),
            Transform(bit1, zero_bit1_w)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Transition 010 -> 011
        new_bit1_w2 = Text("1", font_size=60, color=WHITE)
        new_bit1_w2.move_to(bit1)
        self.play(Transform(bit1, new_bit1_w2))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight Line 3
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_LINE3)
        )
        
        # Lightbulbs graphic (Off state)
        def create_bulb(color=GRAY):
            bulb_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8)
            bulb_base = Rectangle(height=0.15, width=0.2, color=color, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(bulb_circle, DOWN, buff=0.05)
            return VGroup(bulb_circle, bulb_base)

        bulb3 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb2 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        bulb1 = create_bulb(GRAY)
        
        bulbs_group = VGroup(bulb3, bulb2, bulb1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        self.place_in_area(bulbs_group, "E2", "F5")
        
        # Bit labels below bulbs
        l3 = Text("Bit 3", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb3, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l2 = Text("Bit 2", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb2, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        l1 = Text("Bit 1", font_size=20, color=WHITE).next_to(bulb1, DOWN, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(bulbs_group), FadeIn(l3), FadeIn(l2), FadeIn(l1))
        
        # Pulsing Sequence: 011(3) -> 100(4) -> 101(5) -> 110(6) -> 111(7) -> 000(0)
        curr_val = 3
        for _ in range(5):
            curr_val = (curr_val + 1) % 8
            b_str = format(curr_val, '03b')
            
            # Prepare next bit texts
            next_t3 = Text(b_str[0], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit3)
            next_t2 = Text(b_str[1], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit2)
            next_t1 = Text(b_str[2], font_size=60, color=WHITE).move_to(bit1)
            
            # Bulb colors: COLOR_LINE3 for ON, GRAY for OFF
            target_c3 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[0] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c2 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[1] == '1' else GRAY
            target_c1 = COLOR_LINE3 if b_str[2] == '1' else GRAY
            
            self.play(
                Transform(bit3, next_t3),
                Transform(bit2, next_t2),
                Transform(bit1, next_t1),
                bulb3.animate.set_color(target_c3),
                bulb2.animate.set_color(target_c2),
                bulb1.animate.set_color(target_c1),
                run_time=0.7
            )
            self.wait(0.1)

        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Map each disk to a specific binary bit.",
            "The smallest disk corresponds to the rightmost bit.",
            "Second disk maps to the second binary bit.",
            "The largest disk maps to the third bit.",
            "Move the disk when its bit changes value."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mapping: Disks as Bits", lecture_lines)
        
        MAGENTA = "#FF00FF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Disks (Colored initially as requested in magenta or default?)
        # Storyboard says "Align ... in magenta"
        disk3 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.5, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, color=MAGENTA, fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk2 = RoundedRectangle(width=1.1, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, color=MAGENTA, fill_opacity=0.8)
        disk1 = RoundedRectangle(width=0.7, height=0.4, corner_radius=0.1, color=MAGENTA, fill_opacity=0.8)
        
        d3_label = Text("Disk 3", font_size=20, color=MAGENTA)
        d2_label = Text("Disk 2", font_size=20, color=MAGENTA)
        d1_label = Text("Disk 1", font_size=20, color=MAGENTA)
        
        self.place_at_grid(disk3, "A2")
        self.place_at_grid(d3_label, "A1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk2, "B2")
        self.place_at_grid(d2_label, "B1")
        self.place_at_grid(disk1, "C2")
        self.place_at_grid(d1_label, "C1")
        
        # Bits
        bit3_label = MathTex("2^2", color=MAGENTA)
        bit2_label = MathTex("2^1", color=MAGENTA)
        bit1_label = MathTex("2^0", color=MAGENTA)
        
        self.place_at_grid(bit3_label, "A5")
        self.place_at_grid(bit2_label, "B5")
        self.place_at_grid(bit1_label, "C5")
        
        mapping_arrows = VGroup(
            Arrow(self.grid["A2"], self.grid["A5"], color=MAGENTA, buff=0.8),
            Arrow(self.grid["B2"], self.grid["B5"], color=MAGENTA, buff=0.6),
            Arrow(self.grid["C2"], self.grid["C5"], color=MAGENTA, buff=0.4),
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeIn(disk1, disk2, disk3, d1_label, d2_label, d3_label),
            FadeIn(bit1_label, bit2_label, bit3_label),
            Create(mapping_arrows)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Highlight Disk 1 and Bit 0 (2^0), others to white
        self.play(
            disk2.animate.set_color(WHITE), d2_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            disk3.animate.set_color(WHITE), d3_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            bit2_label.animate.set_color(WHITE), bit3_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            mapping_arrows[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), mapping_arrows[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Highlight Disk 2 and Bit 1 (2^1), others to white
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.set_color(WHITE), d1_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            disk2.animate.set_color(MAGENTA), d2_label.animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            bit1_label.animate.set_color(WHITE), bit2_label.animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            mapping_arrows[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), mapping_arrows[1].animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Highlight Disk 3 and Bit 2 (2^2), others to white
        self.play(
            disk2.animate.set_color(WHITE), d2_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            disk3.animate.set_color(MAGENTA), d3_label.animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            bit2_label.animate.set_color(WHITE), bit3_label.animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            mapping_arrows[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), mapping_arrows[0].animate.set_color(MAGENTA),
            run_time=1
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(MAGENTA)
        
        # Reset colors for transition
        self.play(
            disk3.animate.set_color(WHITE), d3_label.animate.set_color(WHITE),
            bit3_label.animate.set_color(WHITE), mapping_arrows[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
        )
        
        # Clear mapping visual
        self.play(
            FadeOut(mapping_arrows),
            FadeOut(d1_label, d2_label, d3_label),
            FadeOut(bit1_label, bit2_label, bit3_label)
        )
        
        # Setup Tower at the bottom
        peg_base = Line(self.grid["F1"], self.grid["F6"], color=WHITE)
        pegA = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=1.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(self.grid["E2"])
        pegB = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=1.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(self.grid["E4"])
        pegC = Rectangle(width=0.1, height=1.2, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=1).move_to(self.grid["E6"])
        
        # Binary Counter at D4-D6
        bit3_val = Text("0", font_size=36).move_to(self.grid["D4"])
        bit2_val = Text("0", font_size=36).move_to(self.grid["D5"])
        bit1_val = Text("0", font_size=36).move_to(self.grid["D6"])
        counter_labels = VGroup(
            MathTex("2^2", font_size=24).next_to(bit3_val, UP),
            MathTex("2^1", font_size=24).next_to(bit2_val, UP),
            MathTex("2^0", font_size=24).next_to(bit1_val, UP)
        )
        
        # Stack disks on Peg A
        # Disk 3 at bottom, then 2, then 1.
        self.play(
            Create(peg_base), Create(pegA), Create(pegB), Create(pegC),
            FadeIn(bit3_val, bit2_val, bit1_val, counter_labels),
            disk3.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*0.2),
            disk2.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*0.6),
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["F2"] + UP*1.0)
        )
        
        # Bit 2^0 flips: 0 -> 1
        new_bit1_val = Text("1", font_size=36, color=MAGENTA).move_to(self.grid["D6"])
        
        self.play(
            Transform(bit1_val, new_bit1_val),
            disk1.animate.set_color(MAGENTA)
        )
        
        # Move Disk 1 to Peg C
        path_points = [
            disk1.get_center(),
            self.grid["C4"], # Midway UP
            self.grid["F6"] + UP*0.2 # Destination
        ]
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C2"] + UP*2), # Lift
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["C6"] + UP*2), # Shift
            run_time=0.5
        )
        self.play(
            disk1.animate.move_to(self.grid["F6"] + UP*0.2), # Drop
            run_time=0.5
        )
        
        self.wait(2)

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            fill_color=COLOR_GOLD,

        )

        self.wait(2)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Initialize the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1", [
            "- Binary counting perfectly models the Tower of Hanoi.",
            "- Total moves equal two to the power n minus one.",
            "- Each move is encoded in the binary sequence."
        ])

        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.place_in_area(formula, 'B2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.8)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"),

        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Demonstrate the magnitude for n = 64 disks.
        # Show n = 64 and the resulting massive number of moves below it.
        # Text '585 Billion Years' appears and slowly scales up in white #FFFFFF.
        
        n_display = MathTex("n = 64", color=WHITE)
        # Representing 2^64 - 1
        moves_val = MathTex(r"M = 18,446,744,073,709,551,615", color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(n_display, 'C2', 'C5', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_in_area(moves_val, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        time_text = Text("585 Billion Years", color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(time_text, 'F2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            FadeIn(n_display, shift=UP),
            FadeIn(moves_val, shift=UP)
        )
        self.wait(1.5)
        
        # Final dramatic reveal of the time scale
        self.play(
            FadeIn(time_text),
            time_text.animate.scale(1.4),
            run_time=3,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: The Binary Secret of the Tower of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students and early undergraduate computer science students

sections.title: The Puzzle Setup: Rules of the Game
sections.content: Introduce the Tower of Hanoi components: three vertical pegs and a stack of 'n' disks of different sizes. Explain the two core rules: 1. Only one disk can be moved at a time. 2. A larger disk can never be placed on top of a smaller disk. Establish the goal: move the entire stack to a different peg in the minimum number of moves.
sections.example: A curious robot named 'Alpha' is trying to move 3 golden pancakes from Peg A to Peg C without ever squashing a smaller pancake.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Binary Counting as a Pulse
sections.content: Visualize binary counting as a sequence of bits flipping. Explain that in a binary number, each position (bit) represents a power of 2. Show a 3-bit counter (000 to 111) and highlight which specific bit changes during each increment. Use a 'lightbulb' graphic where 'Off' is 0 and 'On' is 1.
sections.example: Sequence: 000 -> 001 (Bit 1 flips) -> 010 (Bit 1 and 2 flip) -> 011 (Bit 1 flips). Notice that Bit 1 flips every 1 step, Bit 2 every 2 steps, and Bit 3 every 4 steps.

sections.title: The Mapping: Disks as Bits
sections.content: Create a one-to-one mapping between the binary bits and the disks. Disk 1 (smallest) corresponds to the rightmost bit (2^0). Disk 2 corresponds to the second bit (2^1), and so on. Explain the 'Magic Rule': Whenever a bit in the binary counter changes its value (0 to 1 or 1 to 0), the corresponding disk must be moved.
sections.example: In a 3-disk game, counting from 0 to 7 in binary (000 to 111) provides the exact timing for every move. When the counter goes from 000 to 001, Bit 1 changes, so we move Disk 1.

sections.title: The Directional Logic: Where to Move?
sections.content: Explain the spatial logic using a cyclic movement pattern. For an odd number of disks: move the smallest disk in the cycle A -> C -> B -> A. For an even number: A -> B -> C -> A. All other disks move to the only available legal position. This ensures the binary 'flip' always results in a valid move.
sections.example: Graphic: A triangular path showing Pegs A, B, and C. When the binary counter hits '001', Disk 1 (the smallest) follows the arrow from A to C.

sections.title: Synthesis: Solving the 3-Disk Puzzle
sections.content: Walk through the full 7-step solution ($2^3 - 1$) by incrementing the binary counter. Show a split-screen: left side increments binary (001, 010, 011...), right side animates the corresponding disk move. Emphasize that the 'rightmost changed bit' always identifies the disk to be moved.
sections.example: At Step 4 (binary 100), the 3rd bit is the rightmost bit that changed from the previous state (011). Therefore, we move Disk 3 (the largest).

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of 2^n - 1
sections.content: Summarize why binary counting is the perfect mathematical model for this recursive problem. Introduce the formula for total moves: $M = 2^n - 1$. Explain that the binary representation of the move number tells you exactly which disk is currently in motion.
sections.example: If you had 64 disks like the Monks in the original legend, the binary counter would reach a number with 64 ones, taking $2^{64}-1$ moves—roughly 585 billion years!
